title: Heterogeneous treatment effects by firm size in DID

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The research question asks whether a corporate tax cut (effective from period 4) differentially affected investment for large versus small firms. We have panel data on firms over time, with large firms (`treated = 1`) experiencing a larger tax cut compared to small firms (`treated = 0`).

The appropriate causal method is **Difference-in-Differences (DID)**.
This method is suitable because:
1.  We have a clearly defined intervention (the larger corporate tax cut for large firms) that occurred at a specific point in time (beginning of period 4).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with heterogeneous effects — triple-diff or interaction terms for size groups
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Large firms increase investment more than small firms post tax cut
_ground_truth.main_effect: 28% higher investment growth for large firms
